Implementation Plan

Reviewer prompt component logging for the reviewer pipeline — implementation plan

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8845` @ `fb7c793795ecf11e7a5856536e609cdc63c06412` (integration branch mismatch: false). Orchestrator child of tracking issue #8845; PR text must use `Refs #8845`, never a closing keyword.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends gh_api_json_to_file
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for measurement only: one log line for each assembled reviewer prompt, with no change to prompt bytes, order or budgets. The plan reuses the 12-hex sha pattern from `gh_api_json_to_file` in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` (lines 1445-1448: `sha256sum < f | cut -c1-12`, falling back to `shasum -a 256`). It also reuses the `wc -c ... | tr -d '[:space:]'` plus `^[0-9]+$` check that the existing size log already uses (`scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` ~3292-3295). The complete option costs only a few more lines than a single call site, so it covers all three assembly call sites (default, pass 1, pass 2). §6 order (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed) favours that completeness. Nothing in the existing assembly is refactored.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`
- `tests/test_review_reviewer_prompt_components.py` (new)
- `agents.d/wfopt-2026-10-02-reviewer-prompt-components.md` (new)
- `changelog.d/wfopt-2026-10-02-reviewer-prompt-components.md` (new)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Automation / scheduler surface (§20.E)
- No new script. This extends an existing helper only.
- Entry point: the existing "Run reviewer models" step of `review_autofix.yml`, which runs `review_run_reviewers.sh` on PR review. No new wiring is needed.
- No supervisor, no DB work and no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.

## Functions or modules to implement
1. **`log_reviewer_prompt_components` in `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`** (new; `grep -n "reviewer_prompt_component\|log_reviewer_prompt" scripts/*.sh` found no match).
   - Placement: directly after the closing `}` of `assemble_reviewer_prompt()` (~line 3278), before the `# Assemble the default (pass 1 / single-pass) prompt.` comment.
     - `tests/test_review_semble_contract.py` (lines 331/357) slices from `assemble_reviewer_prompt()` up to `# Assemble the default`. The helper then sits inside that slice as a harmless definition.
     - The `append_reviewer_checklist_block()` → `# Assemble the base reviewer prompt` slice is not affected.
   - Signature: `log_reviewer_prompt_components <pass_label> <assembled_file> <prompt_body_file> [extra_context_file]`.
   - Sub-helper `reviewer_prompt_component_bytes <path>`:
     - Prints `0` for an empty path, a path that is not a regular file, or an unreadable file.
     - Otherwise prints `wc -c < path 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]'`, with `|| printf '0'`.
     - Any value not matching `^[0-9]+$` becomes `0`.
     - Check this name is also unique before adding it.
   - Inputs, mirroring exactly what `assemble_reviewer_prompt` reads:
     - `static_bytes`: `${REVIEWER_STATIC_CONTEXT_PATH:-./pre_assembled_static.txt}`
     - `readme_bytes`: `${RUNTIME_DIR}/static_readme_trimmed.txt`, only when `RUNTIME_DIR` is non-empty; otherwise 0. This is the raw file size, before the `UNTRUSTED_DATA:` framing.
     - `memory_bytes`: `${MEMORY_CONTEXT_FILE:-}`
     - `body_bytes`: `$3`
     - `semble_bytes`: `${REVIEWER_SEMBLE_CONTEXT_FILE:-}`
     - `extra_bytes`: `${4:-}`
     - `total_bytes`: `$2`, the assembled file
   - `static_prefix_sha256`:
     - Use `sha256sum` if `command -v sha256sum` finds it, else `shasum -a 256`. Read the static file on stdin and keep `cut -c1-12`, with `|| true`.
     - Accept the result only if it matches `^[0-9a-f]{12}$`; otherwise print `unavailable`. A missing or unreadable static file also gives `unavailable`.
   - `pass`: printed as given only if it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`, else `unknown`.
   - Output:
     - Build the whole line in one local variable, then write it with one `printf '%s\n'` to stdout, like the existing size line.
     - Line: `REVIEWER_PROMPT_COMPONENTS pass=<label> static_bytes=<int> readme_bytes=<int> memory_bytes=<int> body_bytes=<int> semble_bytes=<int> extra_bytes=<int> total_bytes=<int> static_prefix_sha256=<12hex|unavailable>`
     - The helper never prints file content, file paths or the label when the label fails the check.
   - All locals use the `local` keyword, and every variable read uses the `${VAR:-}` form, because the script runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 2).
2. **Call sites.** Each call is wrapped so a failure gives exactly one warning and does not change the exit status:
   `if ! log_reviewer_prompt_components <label> ...; then echo "::warning::REVIEWER_PROMPT_COMPONENTS could not be computed for pass=<label>; continuing (log-only)."; fi`
   - The `if !` context suspends errexit inside the function. Every sub-command already has a fallback, and the single print happens last, so a failure prints nothing before the warning.
   - **default** (label `default`, files `"${REVIEWER_PROMPT_FILE}" "${REVIEWER_PROMPT_BODY_FILE}"`):
     - Goes inside the existing `if [ -f "${REVIEWER_PROMPT_FILE}" ]; then` block (~3291), after the cap-warning `fi`.
     - The existing `Reviewer prompt assembled size:` line and the `::warning::Reviewer prompt is ...` text stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
   - **pass1** (label `pass1`): directly after `assemble_reviewer_prompt "${PASS1_PROMPT_FILE}" "${REVIEWER_PROMPT_BODY_FILE}"` (~5998), before `run_reviewer_pass`.
   - **pass2** (label `pass2`, extra `"${CROSS_POLLINATION_FILE}"`): directly after `assemble_reviewer_prompt "${PASS2_PROMPT_FILE}" "${REVIEWER_PROMPT_BODY_FILE}" "${CROSS_POLLINATION_FILE}"` (~6109).
   - None of these sits inside a `$( )` capture, so the line goes to the step log rather than into a variable.
3. **CI wiring.** Add `tests/test_review_reviewer_prompt_components.py \` to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in the "Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 2)" list (group 4, ~line 2645). Put it in alphabetical order after `tests/test_review_reviewer_common_context_sections.py`, so `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` passes. `ci.yml` is 171,577 bytes, well under the 480,000-byte guard.
4. **agents.d fragment.** One block under `<!-- agents: section="Stable log prefixes (contractual)" -->`:
   - A `` - `REVIEWER_PROMPT_COMPONENTS` `` bullet covering:
     - the source (`scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`, `log_reviewer_prompt_components`) and the three `pass` labels (`default`, `pass1`, `pass2`, else `unknown`);
     - the field list and value domains;
     - that `readme_bytes` is the raw trimmed file before framing;
     - that the component sum does not equal `total_bytes`, because separators, hints, the memory placeholder and the checklist are not counted separately;
     - that the line is log-only and fail-open.
   - The line `LOG_PREFIX.name=REVIEWER_PROMPT_COMPONENTS`.
   - Format follows `agents.d/wfopt-2026-10-02-reviewer-malformed-class.md`.
5. **changelog.d fragment.** `<!-- changelog: changed -->` marker (same precedent as `changelog.d/wfopt-2026-10-02-reviewer-malformed-class.md`) with one bullet describing the new line, ending in `Refs #8845.`

## Data structures affected
- None persisted. One new stdout log line per assembled prompt. No env vars, files, budgets or exit codes change.

## API or interface changes
- New contractual log prefix `REVIEWER_PROMPT_COMPONENTS`, registered through the agents.d fragment.
- The existing `Reviewer prompt assembled size:` line and the cap warning are unchanged.

Failure modes:
- `wc` or `sha256sum` missing or failing: the count falls back to `0` and the sha to `unavailable`; the line still prints.
- The helper's final `printf` fails (for example a closed stdout): one `::warning::` line, then the script continues with an unchanged exit status.
- The static context file is missing: `static_bytes=0 static_prefix_sha256=unavailable`. `assemble_reviewer_prompt` keeps its existing behaviour; the helper runs only after it.

## Decisions
### D1 — Helper placement right after `assemble_reviewer_prompt()`
- Chosen: define `log_reviewer_prompt_components` and `reviewer_prompt_component_bytes` between the `assemble_reviewer_prompt` closing brace and `# Assemble the default`.
- Alternatives considered: inside `assemble_reviewer_prompt`, which would change the function the semble and checklist tests run; or after the default size log, which would leave the helper undefined if the order changed.
- Why: it is defined before all three call sites, leaves the assembly body untouched, and sits harmlessly inside the semble test slice.
### D2 — Fail-open by building one string and using an `if !` guard at the call site
- Chosen: compute every field with a local fallback, print once, and have the caller emit a single `::warning::` when the call returns nonzero.
- Alternatives considered: `|| true` with no warning (hides failures); `trap` (too much machinery and could leak into the outer `set -e` context).
- Why: issue requirement 4 says "single warning and nothing else" and no exit-status change.
### D3 — Pass labels `default` / `pass1` / `pass2`
- Chosen: name each label after its assembly call site.
- Alternatives considered: reusing `REVIEWER_ATTEMPT_RESULT`'s `pass1`/`review`.
- Why: the default single-pass assembly and pass 2 are separate prompts. Distinct labels keep the per-prompt byte counts unambiguous. The labels are documented in the fragment.
### D4 — Counted files are the raw inputs
- Chosen: `wc -c` on the input files as the issue specifies (README raw, memory 0 when its file is empty).
- Alternatives considered: measuring framed output segments.
- Why: the issue asks for `wc -c` on the existing files, and measuring framed segments would need changes to the assembly.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the README, memory, semble and cross-poll
